lines.text: If you're giving a talk that requires persuading an audience to see something differently,
the key is to take the journey one step at a time.
Prime your listener's mind for a change.
Once an audience has been primed, it's much easier to make your main argument,
even if it contradicts an idea the audience held true.
By using reasoning, you can show how and why something is true.
Each true assumption leads to a conclusion that must then also be true.
Another kind of reasoned argument is the detective story.
Some of the most persuasive TED Talks are set up like detective stories.
You start with the big mystery,
then travel the world of ideas in search of possible solutions to it,
ruling them out one by one, until there's only one solution left.
It can sometimes be hard to make reason-based talks really exciting to listen to.
Most people can be convinced by reason, but it doesn't always leave them feeling energized.
So if you plan to use reason to persuade your audience,
you may have to pick up some other tools as well.
